concept.name: Sideways market
concept.definition: A market state in which prices oscillate within a horizontal band with roughly equal peaks and troughs, reflecting a balance between supply and demand rather than directional movement. Also described as consolidation or a ranging market; a descriptive label for price behavior, not a forecast.
concept.intuition: Buyers and sellers are evenly matched, so price ping-pongs between an upper and a lower boundary.
concept.mechanics: Identified when swing highs cluster near a common resistance level and swing lows near a common support level with no sustained progression in either direction. The state is considered resolved when price breaks decisively out of the band.
concept.failure_modes: Range boundaries are approximate, so price frequently pokes through them intraday before returning, whipsawing traders who treat every touch of the edge as meaningful.
concept.misconceptions: That sideways markets are low-risk because they are quiet; ranges often precede sharp directional moves, and volatility can expand abruptly.
concept.example: A stock bounces between $70 support and $75 resistance for several weeks without closing outside the band.
